entries.8a44de4d5ac75a346d533f3fb60b5b9212ee4e09: <div sID="gen34186" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="16" osisID="Rev.16" sID="Rev.16"/> <div eID="gen34186" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34187" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34188" type="x-p"/> In this chapter we have an account of the pouring forth of these vials that were filled with the wrath of God. They were poured out upon the whole antichristian empire, and on every thing appertaining to it. I. Upon the earth, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.2">ver. 2</reference>. II. Upon the sea, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.3">ver. 3</reference>. III. Upon the rivers and fountains of water, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.4">ver. 4</reference>. Here the heavenly hosts proclaim and applaud the righteousness of the judgments of God. IV. The fourth vial was poured out on the sun, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.8">ver. 8</reference>. V. The fifth on the seat of the beast. VI. The sixth on the river Euphrates. VII. The seventh in the air, upon which the cities of the nations fell, and great Babylon came in remembrance before God.
entries.947251c4fb9448b003faeacde5803bee56a4dcc8: <div eID="gen34188" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34187" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Seven Vials. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34189" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And I heard a great voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth. <hi type="super">2</hi> And the first went, and poured out his vial upon the earth; and there fell a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and <hi type="italic">upon</hi> them which worshipped his image. <hi type="super">3</hi> And the second angel poured out his vial upon the sea; and it became as the blood of a dead <hi type="italic">man:</hi> and every living soul died in the sea. 4 And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and fountains of waters; and they became blood. <hi type="super">5</hi> And I heard the angel of the waters say, Thou art righteous, O Lord, which art, and wast, and shalt be, because thou hast judged thus. 6 For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy. <hi type="super">7</hi> And I heard another out of the altar say, Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy judgments. <div eID="gen34189" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34190" type="x-p"/> We had in the foregoing chapter the great and solemn preparation that was made for the pouring out of the vials; now we have the performance of that work. Here observe, <div eID="gen34190" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34191" type="x-p"/> I. That, though every thing was made ready before, yet nothing was to be put in execution without an immediate positive order from God; and this he gave out of the temple, answering the prayers of his people, and avenging their quarrel. <div eID="gen34191" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34192" type="x-p"/> II. No sooner was the word of command given than it was immediately obeyed; no delay, no objection made. We find that some of the best men, as Moses and Jeremiah, did not so readily come in and comply with the call of God to their work; but the angels of God excel not only in strength, but in a readiness to do the will of God. God says, <hi type="italic">Go your ways, and pour out the vials,</hi> and immediately the work is begun. We are taught to pray that the will of God may be done on earth as it is done in heaven. And now we enter upon a series of very terrible dispensations of Providence, of which it is difficult to give the certain meaning or to make the particular application. But in the general it is worth our observation that, <div eID="gen34192" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34193" type="x-p"/> 1. We have here a reference and allusion to several of the plagues of Egypt, such as the turning of their waters into blood, and smiting them with boils and sores. Their sins were alike, and so were their punishments. <div eID="gen34193" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34194" type="x-p"/> 2. These vials have a plain reference to the seven trumpets, which represented the rise of antichrist; and we learn hence that the fall of the church's enemies shall bear some resemblance to their rise, and that God can bring them down in such ways as they chose to exalt themselves. And the fall of antichrist shall be gradual; as Rome was not built in one day, so neither shall it fall in one day, but it falls by degrees; it shall fall so as to rise no more. <div eID="gen34194" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34195" type="x-p"/> 3. The fall of the antichristian interest shall be universal. Every thing that any ways belonged to them, or could be serviceable to them, the premises and all their appurtenances, are put into the writ for destruction: their earth, their air, their sea, their rivers, their cities, all consigned over to ruin, all accursed for the sake of the wickedness of that people. Thus the creation groans and suffers through the sins of men. Now we proceed to, <div eID="gen34195" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34196" type="x-p"/> (1.) The first angel who poured out his vial, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.2">v. 2</reference>. Observe, [1.] Where it fell—<hi type="italic">upon the earth;</hi> that is, say some, upon the common people; others upon the body of the Romish clergy, who were the basis of the papacy, and of an earthly spirit, all carrying on earthly designs. [2.] What it produced—<hi type="italic">noisome and grievous sores on all who had the mark of the beast.</hi> They had marked themselves by their sin; now God marks them out by his judgments. This sore, some think, signifies some of the first appearances of Providence against their state and interest which gave them great uneasiness, as it discovered their inward distemper and was a token of further evil; the plague—tokens appeared. <div eID="gen34196" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34197" type="x-p"/> (2.) <hi type="italic">The second angel poured out his vial;</hi> and here we see, [1.] Where it fell—<hi type="italic">upon the sea;</hi> that is, say some, upon the jurisdiction and dominion of the papacy; others upon the whole system of their religion, their false doctrines, their corrupt glosses, their superstitious rites, their idolatrous worship, their pardons, indulgences, a great conflux of wicked inventions and institutions, by which they maintain a trade and traffic advantageous to themselves, but injurious to all who deal with them. [2.] What it produced: It turned the sea into blood, <hi type="italic">as the blood of a dead man, and every living soul died in the sea.</hi> God discovered not only the vanity and falsehood of their religion, but the pernicious and deadly nature of it—that the souls of men were poisoned by that which was pretended to be the sure means of their salvation. <div eID="gen34197" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34198" type="x-p"/> (3.) The next angel poured out his vial; and we are told, [1.] Where it fell—<hi type="italic">upon the rivers, and upon the fountains of waters;</hi> that is, say some very learned men, upon their emissaries, and especially the Jesuits, who, like streams, conveyed the venom and poison of their errors and idolatries from the spring-head through the earth. [2.] What effect it had upon them: <hi type="italic">It turned them into blood;</hi> some think it stirred up Christian princes to take a just revenge upon those that had been the great incendiaries of the world, and had occasioned the shedding of the blood of armies and of martyrs. The following doxology (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.5-Rev.16.6">v. 5, 6</reference>) favours this sense. The instrument that God makes use of in this work is here called <hi type="italic">the angel of the waters,</hi> who extols the righteousness of God in this retaliation: <hi type="italic">They have shed the blood of thy saints, and thou hast given them blood to drink, for they are worthy,</hi> to which another angel answered by full consent, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.7">v. 7</reference>.
entries.9af6e802a0f514c20dcf6a66f696397197b42e08: <div eID="gen34198" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Seven Vials. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34199" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">8</hi> And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun; and power was given unto him to scorch men with fire. 9 And men were scorched with great heat, and blasphemed the name of God, which hath power over these plagues: and they repented not to give him glory. <hi type="super">10</hi> And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain, <hi type="super">11</hi> And blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds. <div eID="gen34199" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34200" type="x-p"/> In these verses we see the work going on in the appointed order. The fourth angel poured out his vial, and that fell upon the sun; that is, say some, upon some eminent prince of the popish communion, who should renounce their false religion a little while before his utter downfall; and some expect it will be the German emperor. And now what will be the consequence of this? That sun which before cherished them with warm and benign influences shall now grow hot against these idolaters, and shall scorch them. Princes shall use their power and authority to suppress them, which yet will be so far from bringing them to repentance, that it will cause them to curse God and their king, and look upward, throwing out their blasphemous speeches against the God of heaven; they will be hardened to their ruin. The fifth angel poured out his vial, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.10">v. 10</reference>. And observe, 1. Where this fell—<hi type="italic">upon the seat of the beast,</hi> upon Rome itself, the mystical Babylon, the head of the antichristian empire. 2. What effect it had there: The whole kingdom of the beast <hi type="italic">was full of darkness</hi> and distress. That very city which was the seat of their policy, the source of all their learning, and all their knowledge, and all their pomp and pleasure, now becomes a source of darkness, and pain, and anguish. Darkness was one of the plagues of Egypt, and it is opposed to lustre and honour, and so forebodes the contempt and scorn to which the antichristian interest should be exposed. Darkness is opposed to wisdom and penetration, and forebodes the confusion and folly which the idolaters should discover at that time. It is opposed to pleasure and joy, and so signifies their anguish and vexation of Spirit, when their calamities thus came upon them.
entries.282234befb601ba744ba8e8146ba55575e2fcb94: <div eID="gen34200" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Seven Vials. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34201" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">12</hi> And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates; and the water thereof was dried up, that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared. <hi type="super">13</hi> And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs <hi type="italic">come</hi> out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet. <hi type="super">14</hi> For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, <hi type="italic">which</hi> go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty. <hi type="super">15</hi> Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed <hi type="italic">is</hi> he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame. <hi type="super">16</hi> And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon. <div eID="gen34201" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34202" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">The sixth angel poured out his vial;</hi> and observe, <div eID="gen34202" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34203" type="x-p"/> I. Where it fell—<hi type="italic">upon the great river Euphrates.</hi> Some take it literally, for the place where the Turkish power and empire began; and they think this is a prophecy of the destruction of the Turkish monarchy and of idolatry, which they suppose will be effected about the same time with that of the papacy, as another antichrist, and that thereby a way shall be made for the conveniency of the Jews, those princes of the east. Others take it for the river Tiber; for, as Rome is mystical Babylon, Tiber is mystical Euphrates. And when Rome shall be destroyed her river and merchandise must suffer with her. <div eID="gen34203" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34204" type="x-p"/> II. What did this vial produce? 1. The drying up of the river, which furnished the city with wealth, provisions, and all sorts of accommodations. 2. A way is hereby prepared <hi type="italic">for the kings of the east.</hi> The idolatry of the church of Rome had been a great hindrance both to the conversion of the Jews, who have been long cured of their inclination to idols, and of the Gentiles, who are hardened in their idolatry by seeing that which so much symbolizes with it among those called Christians. It is therefore very probable that the downfall of popery, removing these obstructions, will open a way for both the Jews and other eastern nations to come into the church of Christ. And, if we suppose that Mahomedism shall fall at the same time, there will be still a more open communication between the western and eastern nations, which may facilitate the conversion of the Jews, and of <hi type="italic">the fulness of the Gentiles.</hi> And when this work of God appears, and is about to be accomplished, no wonder if it occasion another consequence, which is, 3. The last effort of the great dragon; he is resolved to have another push for it, that, if possible, he may retrieve the ruinous posture of his affairs in the world. He is now rallying his forces, recollecting all his spirits, to make one desperate sally before all be lost. This is occasioned by the pouring out of the sixth vial. Here observe, (1.) The instruments he makes use of to engage the powers of the earth in his cause and quarrel: <hi type="italic">Three unclean spirits like frogs</hi> come forth, one <hi type="italic">out of the mouth of the dragon,</hi> another <hi type="italic">out of the mouth of the beast, and</hi> a third <hi type="italic">out of the mouth of the false prophet.</hi> Hell, the secular power of antichrist, and the ecclesiastical power, would combine to send their several instruments, furnished with hellish malice, with worldly policy, and with religious falsehood and deceit; and these would muster up the devil's forces for a decisive battle. (2.) The means these instruments would use to engage the powers of earth in this war. They would work pretended miracles, the old stratagem of him <hi type="italic">whose coming is after the working of Satan, with all power, and signs, and lying wonders, and with all deceivableness of unrighteousness,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Thess.2.9-2Thess.2.10">2 Thess. ii. 9, 10</reference>. Some think that a little before the fall of antichrist the popish pretence of power to work miracles will be revived and will very much amuse and deceive the world. (3.) The field of battle—a place called <hi type="italic">Armageddon;</hi> that is, say some, the mount of Megiddo, near to which, by a stream issuing thence, Barak overcame Sisera, and all the kings in alliance with him, <reference osisRef="Judg.5.19">Judges v. 19</reference>. And in the valley of Megiddo Josiah was slain. This place had been famous for two events of a very different nature, the former very happy for the church of God, the latter very unhappy; but it shall now be the field of the last battle in which the church shall be engaged, and she shall be victorious. This battle required time to prepare for it, and therefore the further account of it is suspended till we come to the nineteenth chapter, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.19-Rev.16.20">v. 19, 20</reference>. (4.) The warning which God gives of this great and decisive trial, to engage his people to prepare for it, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.15">v. 15</reference>. It would be sudden and unexpected, and therefore Christians should be clothed, and armed, and ready for it, that they might not be surprised and ashamed. When God's cause comes to be tried, and his battles to be fought, all his people shall be ready to stand up for his interest and be faithful and valiant in his service.
entries.efbd0409756051861e8b6102dd01f58c67148be5: <div eID="gen34204" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Seven Vials. (<hi type="small-caps">a. d.</hi> 95.)</title> <div sID="gen34205" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">17</hi> And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done. <hi type="super">18</hi> And there were voices, and thunders, and lightnings; and there was a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake, <hi type="italic">and</hi> so great. <hi type="super">19</hi> And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell: and great Babylon came in remembrance before God, to give unto her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath. <hi type="super">20</hi> And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found. 21 And there fell upon men a great hail out of heaven, <hi type="italic">every stone</hi> about the weight of a talent: and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail; for the plague thereof was exceeding great. <div eID="gen34205" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34206" type="x-p"/> Here we have an account of the seventh and last angel pouring forth his vial, contributing his part towards the accomplishment of the downfall of Babylon, which was the finishing stroke. And here, as before, observe, <div eID="gen34206" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34207" type="x-p"/> I. Where this plague fell—<hi type="italic">on the air,</hi> upon the prince of the power of the air, that is, the devil. His powers were restrained, his policies confounded; he was bound in God's chain: the sword of God was upon his eye and upon his arm; for he, as well as the powers of the earth, is subject to the almighty power of God. He had used all possible means to preserve the antichristian interest, and to prevent the fall of Babylon—all the influence that he has upon the minds of men, blinding their judgments and perverting them, hardening their hearts, raising their enmity to the gospel as high as could be. But now here is a vial poured out upon his kingdom, and he is not able to support his tottering cause and interest any longer. <div eID="gen34207" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34208" type="x-p"/> II. What it produced, 1. A thankful voice from heaven, pronouncing that now the work was done. The church triumphant in heaven saw it, and rejoiced; the church militant on earth saw it, and became triumphant. It is finished. 2. A mighty commotion on the earth—an earthquake, so great as never was before, shaking the very centre, and this ushered in by the usual concomitants of thunder and lightnings. 3. The fall of Babylon, which was divided into three parts, <hi type="italic">called the cities of the nations</hi> (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.19">v. 19</reference>); having had rule over the nations, and taken in the idolatry of the nations, incorporating into her religion something of the Jewish, something of the pagan, and something of the Christian religion, she was as three cities in one. God now remembered this great and wicked city. Though for some time he seemed to have forgotten her idolatry and cruelty, yet now he gives unto her <hi type="italic">the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.</hi> And this downfall extended further than to the seat of antichrist; it reached from the centre to the circumference; and every island and every mountain, that seemed by nature and situation the most secured, were carried away in the deluge of this ruin. <div eID="gen34208" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34209" type="x-p"/> III. How the antichristian party were affected with it. Though it fell upon them as a dreadful storm, as if the stones of the city, tossed up into the air, came down upon their heads, like hailstones of a talent weight each, yet they were so far from repenting that they blasphemed that God who thus punished them. Here was a dreadful plague of the heart, a spiritual judgment more dreadful and destructive than all the rest. Observe, 1. The greatest calamities that can befal men will not bring them to repentance without the grace of God working with them. 2. Those that are not made better by the judgments of God are always the worse for them. 3. To be hardened in sin and enmity against God by his righteous judgments is a certain token of utter destruction.  <chapter eID="Rev.16"/> <div eID="gen34209" type="x-p"/>

entries.a0aba5639f8344a43761dada927ef747f5f8f42f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19295"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 16</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Rev.16.1-Rev.16.21">Re 16:1-21</reference>. The Seven Vials and the Consequent Plagues.</title> <div sID="gen42121" type="x-p"/> The trumpets shook the world kingdoms in a longer process; the vials destroy with a swift and sudden overthrow the kingdom of "the beast" in particular who had invested himself with the world kingdom. The Hebrews thought the Egyptian plagues to have been inflicted with but an interval of a month between them severally [Bengel, referring to Seder Olam]. As Moses took ashes from an earthly common furnace, so angels, as priestly ministers in the heavenly temple, take holy fire in sacred vials or bowls, from the heavenly altar to pour down (compare <reference osisRef="Rev.8.5">Re 8:5</reference>). The same heavenly altar which would have kindled the sweet incense of prayer bringing down blessing upon earth, by man's sin kindles the fiery descending curse. Just as the river Nile, which ordinarily is the source of Egypt's fertility, became blood and a curse through Egypt's sin.<div eID="gen42121" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42122" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19295"/><hi type="bold">1. a great voice--</hi>namely, God's. These seven vials (the detailed expansion of the vintage, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.18-Rev.14.20">Re 14:18-20</reference>) being called "the last," must belong to the period just when the term of the beast's power has expired (whence reference is made in them all to the worshippers of the beast as the objects of the judgments), close to the end or coming of the Son of man. The first four are distinguished from the last three, just as in the case of the seven seals and the seven trumpets. The first four are more general, affecting the earth, the sea, springs, and the sun, not merely a portion of these natural bodies, as in the case of the trumpets, but the whole of them; the last three are more particular, affecting the throne of the beast, the Euphrates, and the grand consummation. Some of these particular judgments are set forth in detail in the seventeenth through twentieth chapters.<div eID="gen42122" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42123" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">out of the temple--</hi>B and Syriac omit. But A, C, Vulgate, and Andreas support the words.<div eID="gen42123" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42124" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the vials--</hi>so Syriac and Coptic. But A, B, C, Vulgate, and Andreas read, "the seven vials."<div eID="gen42124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42125" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon--</hi>Greek, "into." <div eID="gen42125" type="x-p"/>
entries.dc45390932cc89f9e58fa4c882632a4b464bdc62: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19296"/><div sID="gen42126" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19296"/><hi type="bold">2. went--</hi>Greek, "went away."<div eID="gen42126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42127" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">poured out--</hi>So the angel cast fire into the earth previous to the series of trumpets (<reference osisRef="Rev.8.5">Re 8:5</reference>).<div eID="gen42127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42128" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon--</hi>so Coptic. But A, B, C, Vulgate, and Syriac read, "into."<div eID="gen42128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42129" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">noisome--</hi>literally, "evil" (compare <reference osisRef="Deut.28.27">De 28:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.28.35">35</reference>). The very same Greek word is used in the Septuagint as here, Greek, "helkos." The reason why the sixth Egyptian plague is the first here is because it was directed against the Egyptian magicians, Jannes and Jambres, so that they could not stand before Moses; and so here the plague is sent upon those who in the beast worship had practiced sorcery. As they submitted to the mark of the beast, so they must bear the mark of the avenging God. Contrast <reference osisRef="Rev.7.3">Re 7:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.9.4">Eze 9:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.9.6">6</reference>.<div eID="gen42129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42130" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grievous--</hi>distressing to the sufferers.<div eID="gen42130" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42131" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sore upon the men--</hi>antitype to the sixth Egyptian plague.<div eID="gen42131" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42132" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">which had the mark of the beast--</hi>Therefore this first vial is subsequent to the period of the beast's rule. <div eID="gen42132" type="x-p"/>

But A, B, C, Vulgate, and Syriac omit it.<div eID="gen42148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42149" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">upon--</hi>not as in <reference osisRef="Rev.16.2">Re 16:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.16.3">3</reference>, "into."<div eID="gen42149" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42150" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sun--</hi>Whereas by the fourth trumpet the sun is darkened (<reference osisRef="Rev.8.12">Re 8:12</reference>) in a third part, here by the fourth vial the sun's bright scorching power is intensified.<div eID="gen42150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42151" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">power was given unto him--</hi>rather, "unto it," the sun.<div eID="gen42151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42152" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">men--</hi>Greek, "the men," namely, those who had the mark of the beast (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.2">Re 16:2</reference>). <div eID="gen42152" type="x-p"/>
entries.03b6c94af40c6a48a84d0418abd12be847620952: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19303"/><div sID="gen42153" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19303"/><hi type="bold">9. men--</hi>Greek, "the men."<div eID="gen42153" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42154" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">repented not to give him glory--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rev.9.20">Re 9:20</reference>). entries.38645799e215c21431a6b66870abba2613c0104b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19304"/><div sID="gen42155" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19304"/><hi type="bold">10. angel--</hi>omitted by A, B, C, Vulgate, and Syriac. But Coptic and Andreas support it.<div eID="gen42155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42156" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seat--</hi>Greek, "throne of the beast": set up in arrogant mimicry of God's throne; the dragon gave his throne to the beast (<reference osisRef="Rev.13.2">Re 13:2</reference>).<div eID="gen42156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">darkness--</hi>parallel to the Egyptian plague of darkness, Pharaoh being the type of Antichrist (compare Notes, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.15.2">Re 15:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.15.3">3</reference>; compare the fifth trumpet, <reference osisRef="Rev.9.2">Re 9:2</reference>).<div eID="gen42157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42158" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">gnawed their tongues for pain--</hi>Greek, "owing to the pain" occasioned by the previous plagues, rendered more appalling by the darkness. Or, as "gnashing of teeth" is one of the accompaniments of hell, so this "gnawing of their tongues" is through rage at the baffling of their hopes and the overthrow of their kingdom. They meditate revenge and are unable to effect it; hence their frenzy [Grotius]. Those in anguish, mental and bodily, bite their lips and tongues. <div eID="gen42158" type="x-p"/>
entries.175174391b5d45f483b447810e2e145f5e011f98: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19305"/><div sID="gen42159" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19305"/><hi type="bold">11. sores--</hi>This shows that each fresh plague was accompanied with the continuance of the preceding plagues: there was an accumulation, not a mere succession, of plagues.<div eID="gen42159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42160" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">repented not--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Rev.16.9">Re 16:9</reference>). <div eID="gen42160" type="x-p"/>
entries.5e2fc0210b72ba1ae9737b61c374016adfb84bcd: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19306"/><div sID="gen42161" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19306"/><hi type="bold">12. angel--</hi>so Coptic and Andreas. A, B, C, Vulgate, and Syriac omit.<div eID="gen42161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42162" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kings of the east--</hi>Greek, "the kings who are from the rising of the sun." Reference to the Euphrates similarly occurs in the sixth trumpet. The drying up of the Euphrates, I think, is to be taken figuratively, as Babylon itself, which is situated on it, is undoubtedly so, <reference osisRef="Rev.17.5">Re 17:5</reference>. The waters of the Euphrates (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.8.7">Is 8:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.8.8">8</reference>) are spiritual Babylon's, that is, the apostate Church's (of which Rome is the chief, though not exclusive representative) spiritual and temporal powers. The drying up of the waters of Babylon expresses the same thing as the ten kings stripping, eating, and burning the whore. The phrase, "way may be prepared for," is that applied to the Lord's coming (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Is 40:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.3.3">Mt 3:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.1.76">Lu 1:76</reference>). He shall come from the East (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.27">Mt 24:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.43.2">Eze 43:2</reference>, "the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the East"): not alone, for His elect transfigured saints of Israel and the Gentiles shall accompany Him, who are "kings and priests unto God" (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.6">Re 1:6</reference>). As the Antichristian ten kings accompany the beast, so the saints accompany as kings the King of kings to the last decisive conflict. De Burgh and others take it of the Jews, who also were designed to be a kingdom of priests to God on earth. They shall, doubtless, become priest-kings in the flesh to the nations in the flesh at His coming. Abraham from the East (if <reference osisRef="Isa.41.2">Is 41:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.8.9">8, 9</reference>, refers to him, and not Cyrus) conquering the Chaldean kings is a type of Israel's victorious restoration to the priest-kingdom. Israel's exodus after the last Egyptian plagues typifies Israel's restoration after the spiritual Babylon, the apostate Church, has been smitten. Israel's promotion to the priest-kingdom after Pharaoh's downfall, and at the Lord's descent at Sinai to establish the theocracy, typifies the restored kingdom of Israel at the Lord's more glorious descent, when Antichrist shall be destroyed utterly. Thus, besides the transfigured saints, Israel secondarily may be meant by "the kings from the East" who shall accompany the "King of kings" returning "from the way of the East" to reign over His ancient people. As to the drying up again of the waters opposing His people's assuming the kingdom, compare <reference osisRef="Isa.10.26">Is 10:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.11.11">11:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.15">15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.10.9-Zech.10.11">Zec 10:9-11</reference>. The name Israel (<reference osisRef="Gen.32.28">Ge 32:28</reference>) implies a prince with God. Compare <reference osisRef="Mic.4.8">Mi 4:8</reference> as to the return of the kingdom to Jerusalem. Durham, several centuries ago, interpreted the drying up of the Euphrates to mean the wasting away of the Turkish power, which has heretofore held Palestine, and so the way being prepared for Israel's restoration. But as Babylon refers to the apostate Church, not to Mohammedanism, the drying up of the Euphrates (answering to Cyrus' overthrow of literal Babylon by marching into it through the dry channel of the Euphrates) must answer to the draining off of the apostate Church's resources, the Roman and Greek corrupt Church having been heretofore one of the greatest barriers by its idolatries and persecutions in the way of Israel's restoration and conversion. The kings of the earth who are earthly (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.14">Re 16:14</reference>), stand in contrast to the kings from the East who are heavenly. <div eID="gen42162" type="x-p"/>
entries.2ca1f12328de98a61a899cbb3a5dbd529de71f64: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19307"/><div sID="gen42163" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19307"/><hi type="bold">13. unclean spirits like frogs--</hi>the antitype to the plague of frogs sent on Egypt. The presence of the "unclean spirit" in the land (Palestine) is foretold, <reference osisRef="Zech.13.2">Zec 13:2</reference>, in connection with idolatrous prophets. Beginning with infidelity as to Jesus Christ's coming in the flesh, men shall end in the grossest idolatry of the beast, the incarnation of all that is self-deifying and God-opposed in the world powers of all ages; having rejected Him that came in the Father's name, they shall worship one that comes in his own, though really the devil's representative; as frogs croak by night in marshes and quagmires, so these unclean spirits in the darkness of error teach lies amidst the mire of filthy lusts. They talk of liberty, but it is not Gospel liberty, but license for lust. There being three, as also seven, in the description of the last and worst state of the Jewish nation, implies a parody of the two divine numbers, three of the Trinity, and seven of the Holy Spirit (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.4">Re 1:4</reference>). Some observe that three frogs were the original arms of France, a country which has been the center of infidelity, socialism, and false spiritualism. A and B read, "as it were frogs," instead of "like frogs," which is not supported by manuscripts. The unclean spirit out of the mouth of the dragon symbolizes the proud infidelity which opposes God and Christ. That out of the beast's mouth is the spirit of the world, which in the politics of men, whether lawless democracy or despotism, sets man above God. That out of the mouth of the false prophet is lying spiritualism and religious delusion, which shall take the place of the harlot when she shall have been destroyed.<div eID="gen42163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42164" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the dragon--</hi>Satan, who gives his power and throne (<reference osisRef="Rev.13.2">Re 13:2</reference>) to the beast.<div eID="gen42164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42165" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">false prophet--</hi>distinct from the harlot, the apostate Church (of which Rome is the chief, though not sole, representative), <reference osisRef="Rev.17.1-Rev.3.16">Re 17:1-3, 16</reference>; and identical with the second beast, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.11-Rev.13.15">Re 13:11-15</reference>, as appears by comparing <reference osisRef="Rev.19.20">Re 19:20</reference> with <reference osisRef="Rev.13.13">Re 13:13</reference>; ultimately consigned to the lake of fire with the first beast; as is also the dragon a little later (<reference osisRef="Rev.20.10">Re 20:10</reference>). The dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, "the mystery of iniquity," form a blasphemous Antitrinity, the counterfeit of "the mystery of godliness" God manifests in Christ, witnessed to by the Spirit. The dragon acts the part of God the Father, assigning his authority to his representative the beast, as the Father assigns His to the Son. They are accordingly jointly worshipped; compare as to the Father and Son, <reference osisRef="John.5.23">Joh 5:23</reference>; as the ten-horned beast has its ten horns crowned with diadems (Greek, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.1">Re 13:1</reference>), so Christ has on His head many diadems. While the false prophet, like the Holy Ghost, speaks not of himself, but tells all men to worship the beast, and confirms his testimony to the beast by miracles, as the Holy Ghost attested similarly to Christ's divine mission. <div eID="gen42165" type="x-p"/>
entries.dde6b5054f43557ff19a4ba7262582659f5ef07b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19308"/><div sID="gen42166" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19308"/><hi type="bold">14. devils--</hi>Greek, "demons."<div eID="gen42166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42167" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">working miracles--</hi>Greek, "signs."<div eID="gen42167" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42168" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">go forth unto--</hi>or "for," that is, to tempt them to the battle with Christ.<div eID="gen42168" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42169" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the kings of the earth and, &c.--</hi>A, B, Syriac, and Andreas omit "of the earth and," which clause is not in any manuscript. Translate, "kings of the whole habitable world," who are "of this world," in contrast to "the kings of (from) the East" (the sun-rising), <reference osisRef="Rev.16.12">Re 16:12</reference>, namely, the saints to whom Christ has appointed a kingdom, and who are "children of light." God, in permitting Satan's miracles, as in the case of the Egyptian magicians who were His instruments in hardening Pharaoh's heart, gives the reprobate up to judicial delusion preparatory to their destruction. As Aaron's rod was changed into a serpent, so were those of the Egyptian magicians. Aaron turned the water into blood; so did the magicians. Aaron brought up frogs; so did the magicians. With the frogs their power ceased. So this, or whatever is antitypical to it, will be the last effort of the dragon, beast, and false prophet.<div eID="gen42169" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42170" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">battle--</hi>Greek, "war"; the final conflict for the kingship of the world described in <reference osisRef="Rev.19.17-Rev.19.21">Re 19:17-21</reference>. <div eID="gen42170" type="x-p"/>
entries.2a3646a6c6cfc6229e997651e5a3c08adcdd1dca: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19309"/><div sID="gen42171" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19309"/>15. The gathering of the world kings with the beast against the Lamb is the signal for Christ's coming; therefore He here gives the charge to be watching for His coming and clothed in the garments of justification and sanctification, so as to be accepted.<div eID="gen42171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42172" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thief--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Matt.24.43">Mt 24:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.3.10">2Pe 3:10</reference>).<div eID="gen42172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42173" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they--</hi>saints and angels.<div eID="gen42173" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42174" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shame--</hi>literally, "unseemliness" (Greek, "aschemosunee"): Greek, <reference osisRef="1Cor.13.5">1Co 13:5</reference>: a different word from the Greek in <reference osisRef="Rev.3.18">Re 3:18</reference> (Greek, "aischunee"). <div eID="gen42174" type="x-p"/>
entries.1656b43a29018a16e3e8ab06d7b82b722f3a0739: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19310"/><div sID="gen42175" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19310"/><hi type="bold">16. he--</hi>rather, "they (the three unclean spirits) gathered them together." If English Version be retained, "He" will refer to God who gives them over to the delusion of the three unclean spirits; or else the sixth angel (<reference osisRef="Rev.16.12">Re 16:12</reference>).<div eID="gen42175" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42176" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Armageddon--</hi>Hebrew, "Har," a mountain, and "Megiddo" in Manasseh in Galilee, the scene of the overthrow of the Canaanite kings by God's miraculous interposition under Deborah and Barak; the same as the great plain of Esdraelon. Josiah, too, as the ally of Babylon, was defeated and slain at Megiddo; and the mourning of the Jews at the time just before God shall interpose for them against all the nations confederate against Jerusalem, is compared to the mourning for Josiah at Megiddo. Megiddo comes from a root, gadad, "cut off," and means slaughter. Compare <reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>, 12, 14, where "the valley of Jehoshaphat" (meaning in Hebrew, "judgment of God") is mentioned as the scene of God's final vengeance on the God-opposing foe. Probably some great plain, antitypical to the valleys of Megiddo and Jehoshaphat, will be the scene. <div eID="gen42176" type="x-p"/>
entries.9b3cb6d75a5f8d3aad24cfc532ccb8cb30418c96: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19311"/><div sID="gen42177" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19311"/><hi type="bold">17. angel--</hi>so Andreas. But A, B, Vulgate, and Syriac omit it.<div eID="gen42177" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42178" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">into--</hi>so Andreas (Greek, "eis"). But A and B, "upon" (Greek, "epi").<div eID="gen42178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42179" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">great--</hi>so B, Vulgate, Syriac, Coptic, and Andreas. But A omits.<div eID="gen42179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42180" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">of heaven--</hi>so B and Andreas But A, Vulgate, Syriac, and Coptic omit.<div eID="gen42180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42181" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">It is done--</hi>"It is come to pass." God's voice as to the final consummation, as Jesus' voice on the cross when the work of expiation was completed, "It is finished." <div eID="gen42181" type="x-p"/>
entries.6802a2388f87d44e6b35e11ccb32a0b33d39a532: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19312"/><div sID="gen42182" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19312"/><hi type="bold">18. voice ... thunders ... lightnings--</hi>A has the order, "lightnings ... voices ... thunders." This is the same close as that of the seven seals and the seven thunders; but with the difference that they do not merely form the conclusion, but introduce the consequence, of the last vial, namely, the utter destruction of Babylon and then of the Antichristian armies.<div eID="gen42182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42183" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">earthquake--</hi>which is often preceded by a lurid state of air, such as would result from the vial poured upon it.<div eID="gen42183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42184" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">men were--</hi>so B, Vulgate, Syriac, and Andreas. But A and Coptic read, "A man was."<div eID="gen42184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42185" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">so mighty--</hi>Greek, "such." <div eID="gen42185" type="x-p"/>
entries.f88d0dba4fc2b1f008a745d27c6dc3972bf5b819: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19313"/><div sID="gen42186" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19313"/><hi type="bold">19. the great city--</hi>the capital and seat of the apostate Church, spiritual Babylon (of which Rome is the representative, if one literal city be meant). The city in <reference osisRef="Rev.11.8">Re 11:8</reference> (see on <reference osisRef="Rev.11.8">Re 11:8</reference>), is probably distinct, namely, Jerusalem under Antichrist (the beast, who is distinct from the harlot or apostate Church). In <reference osisRef="Rev.11.13">Re 11:13</reference> only a tenth of Jerusalem falls whereas here the city (Babylon) "became (Greek) into three parts" by the earthquake.<div eID="gen42186" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42187" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cities of the nations--</hi>other great cities in league with spiritual Babylon.<div eID="gen42187" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42188" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">great ... came in remembrance--</hi>Greek, "Babylon the great was remembered" (<reference osisRef="Rev.18.5">Re 18:5</reference>). It is now that the last call to escape from Babylon is given to God's people in her (<reference osisRef="Rev.18.4">Re 18:4</reference>).<div eID="gen42188" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42189" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fierceness--</hi>the boiling over outburst of His wrath (Greek, "thumou orgees"), compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Rev.14.10">Re 14:10</reference>. <div eID="gen42189" type="x-p"/>
entries.1dc957372040e51e54f9a1522d8df49e07660595: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19314"/><div sID="gen42190" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19314"/>20.
